definitions.title: Critical Points and Local Extrema
definitions.latex: \nabla f(x_0, y_0) = \mathbf{0} \iff f_x(x_0, y_0) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad f_y(x_0, y_0) = 0
definitions.statement: A point (x_0, y_0) in the domain of f is a critical point if either both first partial derivatives vanish or at least one partial derivative fails to exist. Local extrema occur only at critical points or boundary points.
conditions: Point belongs to interior of domain
definitions.explanation: Horizontal tangent plane z = z_0 occurs at stationary critical points.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Necessary condition for interior local extrema of differentiable functions.

definitions.title: Second Derivative Test for Functions of Two Variables
definitions.latex: D = f_{xx}(a, b) f_{yy}(a, b) - [f_{xy}(a, b)]^2
definitions.statement: Let (a, b) be a critical point with continuous second partials. If D > 0 and f_{xx} < 0, f has a local maximum; if D > 0 and f_{xx} > 0, f has a local minimum; if D < 0, f has a saddle point; if D = 0, the test is inconclusive.
definitions.explanation: D is the determinant of the Hessian matrix. Positive D guarantees consistent curvature in all directions, while negative D indicates opposite curvatures (saddle).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Classifies stationary points into local maxima, local minima, and saddle points.
